title: Thy Word Invites Us Nigh
description: Thy Word Invites Us Nigh in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 92, “Hungry, and faint, and poor, Behold us, Lord, again Assembled at thy mercies door, Thy bounty to obtain”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy word in-vites us nigh Or we must starve in-deed; For we no mon-ey have to buy, No right-eous-ness to plead.

lines: For we no money have to buy,
Oh, hear the prayer of faith, and grant
That we may eat, and live.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
